headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors if unstructured processes LlamaFactory outputs in shared workflows; prompt-injection risk is low given no shared channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LlamaFactory has no clipboard, filesystem, MCP, or stdin/stdout surfaces, so direct injection into unstructured is not documented. However, unstructured can read documents/files and may ingest LlamaFactory-generated content if manually bridged or placed in a shared workspace, making a limited prompt-injection pathway plausible.
conditions: IF an operator copies LlamaFactory output into a document that unstructured parses as input, injection becomes possible.
IF both agents are pointed at the same shared folder, content-based instruction hijacking becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate folders.
Disable manual copy-paste between outputs and inputs.
Add a review step before any unstructured-ingested document is reused.
Use file naming conventions that separate generated text from source documents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: unstructured reads files and can egress to allowlisted endpoints, while LlamaFactory has no filesystem or network surfaces. The pair can still leak document contents if operators place sensitive files in a shared workspace and then process them through unstructured; the pathway is plausible in default document-processing workflows, though not directly evidenced for LlamaFactory.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are placed in a shared workspace that unstructured reads, those contents can leave the local boundary.
IF unstructured sends parsed content to its allowlisted endpoints, document text may be exposed outside the operator's system.
mitigations: Restrict unstructured to non-sensitive folders.
Turn off network access at the container or host level for sensitive runs.
Separate source and output directories.
Scan inputs for secrets before processing.
Use a redaction step before any upload or API call.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LlamaFactory cannot write files, modify git, or spawn subprocesses, so it cannot contend for mutable resources with unstructured in the same way. unstructured does write files and spawn subprocesses, but the overlap is mostly read-side from LlamaFactory, making write conflicts unlikely unless an external orchestrator adds shared mutable state.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same directory, file clobbering becomes possible.
IF shared git state is introduced outside these profiles, concurrent mutation conflicts may occur.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Run only one writer at a time.
Mount LlamaFactory read-only.
Avoid shared git repositories for the pair.
Use per-agent output subfolders.

D_cascading_error.rationale: unstructured can consume files and produce downstream document outputs, so if it treats LlamaFactory-generated text as authoritative, errors can propagate into parsed artifacts. LlamaFactory is not documented as a verifier, and unstructured's document-processing role makes this a realistic default workflow risk, though not a direct action-taking chain.
conditions: IF unstructured ingests LlamaFactory output without a verification step, hallucinated or malformed content can be propagated.
IF downstream systems trust unstructured's extracted text as ground truth, the error can cascade into later work products.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents.
Require schema validation on LlamaFactory outputs.
Compare extracted text against source documents.
Flag low-confidence extractions for manual inspection.
Keep unstructured outputs advisory rather than authoritative.

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, EU residency, or retention mismatch is documented for LlamaFactory, while unstructured exposes privacy-policy and docs endpoints and processes documents/images/text. The pair therefore shows only a generic compliance surface, not a proven residency or certification conflict; the other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise workflow exposure, not a single-agent violation.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed through unstructured and then retained or uploaded outside policy, compliance obligations may be implicated.
IF the operator requires a specific residency or retention regime not enforced here, the workflow may violate it.
mitigations: Review the privacy policy before processing regulated data.
Keep regulated documents out of the pair.
Set short retention windows for outputs.
Document the data flow for audits.
Use a local-only workflow for sensitive cases.
